title: Restore resumed sessions through the canonical persisted provider route
before: At parent commit 7fd2f574132fcf8aea71ca485ca489c367fedffe, the Desktop/TUI resume reader independently extracted only top-level provider, base_url, and api_mode values from model_config, then fell back to billing_provider. It did not inspect model_config.gateway_runtime, even though the messaging gateway persisted the most recently executed route there on each turn. Consequently, after a session changed providers, Desktop resume could combine the stored model with a stale first-call billing provider or stale top-level endpoint and wire settings.
after: At commit 33c6ab002d1fac653d7e772025ef7aaab7c83480, Desktop/TUI resume delegates persisted-route selection to the same SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime reader used by CLI resume. That reader prioritizes a provider-bearing nested gateway_runtime route, otherwise retains top-level provider/base_url/api_mode data and fills only a missing provider from a routable billing_provider. Existing downstream endpoint-safety, provider-healing, reasoning, and service-tier handling remains in the Desktop resume path.
diff: The change removes the duplicate route-selection logic and local bare-billing-provider import from tui_gateway/server.py, calls SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime(row), and converts its provider/base_url/api_mode result into resume overrides. It adjusts the canonical reader so billing_provider supplements, rather than loses to, partial top-level route metadata. Two regression tests establish that nested gateway_runtime wins over both a stale first-call billing_provider and stale top-level route keys, while existing tests cover nested/top-level precedence, invalid metadata, bare billing buckets, and routable billing-provider fallback.
